rows where total_invoices >= 5,
two ways:

  df = pd.read_sql("SELECT total_invoice_amount, total_invoices FROM quickbooks__customer_analytics", conn)
  sub = df[df['total_invoices'] >= 5]
  sub['total_invoice_amount'].agg(['min','max','mean','median'])

The two engines treat NULL/NaN in total_invoices differently.

handling (COALESCE / fillna), and re-run BOTH from scratch until
MIN/MAX/MEAN/MEDIAN match to all decimal places. If MEDIAN cannot
match (SQL has no native percentile), continue increasing precision
until SQL approximation converges to pandas.

    df = pd.read_sql_query(f"SELECT * FROM {table_name}", conn)
    print(f"Loaded table: {table_name}")
    print(f"Data shape: {df.shape}")
    
    # Display basic info
    print("\nData Info:")
    print(df.info())
    
    # Display first few rows
    print("\nFirst 5 rows:")
    print(df.head())
else:
    print("No tables found in database")
    df = pd.DataFrame()

cursor.close()
conn.close()

# Separate numeric and categorical columns
if not df.empty:
    numeric_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns.tolist()

    print(f"\nNumeric columns ({len(numeric_cols)}): {numeric_cols}")
